references.text: The same chapter confirms that the covenant is not only with those present but also with future generations, which expands the scope of the covenant.
The Lord made a covenant with Israel at Horeb, and this text refers to the same covenant tradition.
God offers Israel a covenant at Sinai, where they are to be His treasured possession if they keep the covenant.
Moses reads the Book of the Covenant to the people, and they commit themselves to keeping the Lord's words. The blood is sprinkled as a sign of the covenant.
The curses mentioned in connection with the covenant, parallel to 'his curse' referred to in the verse.
The curses that come upon those who break the covenant with the Lord, related to 'his curse' in the text.
God establishes His covenant with Abraham and his descendants, a foundational covenant that is renewed with Israel.
Jeremiah prophesies about a new covenant that the Lord will make with the house of Israel, building on the covenant tradition.
The Letter to the Hebrews quotes Jeremiah's prophecy about the new covenant, showing continuity from the old covenant.
